Tom —

Appreciate the clear notes and the reconciliation table. Quick responses below and we'll follow with suggested redline language from legal: 

- Waterfall ordering: Redwood's current operational precedence applies batching/negative-carryover credits first, then the annual true-up. We can accept explicit contract language that codifies "surge reconciliation occurs prior to annual true-up calculations" — that sounds reasonable and defensible.
- Temporary stabilization buffer: we can offer a 90-day transitional surge buffer with capped exposure; this would be an operational waiver (one-time) rather than a permanent floor change. We will need a clear start date in the order form and that the buffer does not expand to change committed minimums.

Karthik / Markus / Laura — please weigh in on the exact redline phrasing below so I can send a consolidated markup back to Acme. I suspect legal will want a clause that: (a) affirms precedence of surge reconciliation; (b) defines the 90-day buffer mechanics (calculation, cap, and expiration); and (c) states that no other pricing exhibits are amended except as expressly stated.

Next steps: I'll circulate a markup draft by EOD and request a short sync if Acme legal wants to step through the calculation examples.

Subject: Suggested redline language for surge reconciliation and 90-day buffer

Team —

Draft language below for inclusion in Exhibit B. I kept it intentionally narrow to limit precedent risk. Feel free to edit for legal tone: 

1) Surge Reconciliation Precedence
"Notwithstanding any other provision in this Agreement, for the purpose of calculating charges and credits for any Billing Period, the parties agree that any Surge Reconciliation (as defined herein) shall be applied prior to the Annual True-Up. Surge Reconciliation means the process by which Usage that exceeds the baseline monthly usage profile by more than the Surge Threshold (see Exhibit B, Section 2) is reconciled and either credited or billed under the Surge Rate prior to aggregation for Annual True-Up calculations."

2) 90-Day Transitional Surge Buffer
"Upon initial go-live, Customer shall be eligible for a one-time, 90-calendar-day Transitional Surge Buffer, commencing on the Service Start Date set forth in the Order Form. During the Transitional Period, charges for Usage between the baseline and the Buffer Cap shall be billed at the Buffer Rate (as set forth in the table below) and shall not be treated as increases to Commit levels for the purposes of subsequent Annual True-Up calculations. The Transitional Surge Buffer shall automatically expire at the end of the 90-day period and shall not alter Customer's committed minimums or long-term pricing schedule."

3) Non-Precedential & Limited Amendment
"The parties acknowledge and agree that the Transitional Surge Buffer is a limited, non-precedential accommodation and, except as explicitly set forth in a signed amendment to this Agreement, shall not be deemed to modify any other Exhibit or term, including but not limited to Commit levels, minimum fees, or price floors."

I've added a short example table we can paste into Exhibit B that mirrors Acme's SURGE_RECONCILIATION_TABLE.xlsx. Markus / Laura — request legal polish if this approach is acceptable.

Karthik
Head of Pricing Strategy — Redwood Inference
